hebrew: בָּרוּךְ שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם. בָּרוּךְ הוּא. בָּרוּךְ עוֹשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית. בָּרוּךְ אוֹמֵר וְעוֹשֶׂה. בָּרוּךְ גּוֹזֵר וּמְקַיֵּם. בָּרוּךְ מְרַחֵם עַל הָאָרֶץ. בָּרוּךְ מְרַחֵם עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת. בָּרוּךְ מְשַׁלֵּם שָׂכָר טוֹב לִירֵאָיו. בָּרוּךְ חַי לָעַד וְקַיָּם לָנֶצַח. בָּרוּךְ פּוֹדֶה וּמַצִּיל. בָּרוּךְ שְׁמוֹ.
transliteration: Baruch she’amar ve’hayah ha’olam. Baruch hu. Baruch oseh bereishit. Baruch omer ve’oseh. Baruch gozer umekayem. Baruch merachem al ha’aretz. Baruch merachem al habriyot. Baruch meshalem sachar tov liy’re’av. Baruch chai la’ad vekayam lanetzach. Baruch podeh umatzil. Baruch shemo.
english: Blessed is He who spoke, and the world came into being. Blessed is He. Blessed is He who makes the beginning. Blessed is He who speaks and does. Blessed is He who decrees and fulfills. Blessed is He who has mercy on the earth. Blessed is He who has mercy on the creatures. Blessed is He who pays a good reward to those who fear Him. Blessed is He who lives forever and endures to eternity. Blessed is He who redeems and rescues. Blessed is His name.
commentary: This opening of Pesukei Dezimra in the traditional Siddur affirms God as the Creator who brings the world into being through speech. In a Conservative intermediate approach the focus is on the kavannah of acknowledging divine creative power at the start of the morning praises, connecting the words to our own speech and actions throughout the day.
kavannahPrompt: As you begin Pesukei Dezimra, pause on the words 'who spoke and the world came into being.' What does it mean for you today that creation continues through divine speech?
